title: Getting Around Uralsk: A First-Year Guide
paragraphs: Uralsk — officially called Oral in Kazakh — is a city of about 260,000 people in western Kazakhstan. It sits at the confluence of the Ural and Chagan rivers, and much of its character comes from this geographical position: it is a river city, and the rivers shape everything from the layout of the streets to the social life of its residents. For new students arriving at WKU, understanding how to navigate the city is one of the first practical challenges they face.

The university campus is located in the northern part of the city, on Dostyq Avenue. From the main dormitory, students can walk to most lecture buildings in under ten minutes. The central library is on the same avenue, just past the main fountain, and the sports hall is behind the administration building, across the car park. For most daily academic needs, students rarely need to leave the campus.

The city centre — known locally as the Old Town area — is about twenty minutes by bus from the university. Students who want to explore Uralsk's cafés, shops, and cultural institutions usually take Bus 5, which stops directly in front of the main gate. The bus runs every fifteen minutes during the day and every thirty minutes in the evening. A single ticket costs 90 tenge.

One of the most useful landmarks for orientation is the Central Mosque, which is visible from many parts of the city. When students ask for directions, locals often use it as a reference point: "Turn left at the mosque" or "It's just past the mosque on the right." The Pushkin Museum, which commemorates the Russian poet's visit to the region in 1833, is another landmark that appears regularly in directions.

The Ural River divides the city. The WKU campus and most student accommodation are on the western bank. The eastern bank is less developed but has some excellent markets and a popular park. To cross from one bank to the other, students use the Central Bridge, which is walkable in about eight minutes, or the Northern Bridge, which is reached by Bus 3. Both bridges offer scenic views of the river and, in winter, of the frozen water and ice fishermen.

Getting around at night requires some planning. Most buses stop running after 10 p.m., and taxis are the main option after that. The city has no metro and limited night transport. However, the university area is compact and safe, and most students find they can walk between the dormitory, the main building, and the nearest convenience stores without difficulty.

For students from larger cities, Uralsk sometimes feels small. For those from smaller towns, it feels like a city. In either case, most students agree that within two or three weeks of arrival, the city becomes familiar. The streets feel readable, the bus routes feel logical, and the landmarks become old friends. Navigation, like language, improves with practice.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Rustam, do you know where the nearest ATM is?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Yes — there's one in the main building, on the ground floor. Just inside the entrance, on the left.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: And is there one near the city centre? I need to get there anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: There's one on the corner of the main square — opposite the museum, next to a pharmacy.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: How do I get to the city centre from here?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Take Bus 5 from outside the main gate. Get off at the Central Mosque stop. Everything is within walking distance of there.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: Does it run in the evening?

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Until about 10. After that you'll need a taxi. The app works well here.

vocab.example: The Central Mosque is one of the most useful landmarks for orientation.

vocab.definition: the ability to know where you are in relation to your surroundings
vocab.example: The mosque helps with orientation — it's visible from many parts of the city.

vocab.definition: to provide space or lodging for someone
vocab.example: The dormitory can accommodate over 2,000 students.

vocab.definition: providing beautiful views of natural scenery
vocab.example: Both bridges offer scenic views of the river in all seasons.

vocab.definition: closely and neatly packed; small but well-organised
vocab.example: The university area is compact and students can walk between buildings easily.

vocab.definition: to do something special to remember a person or event
